purpose: Provider-aligned routing contract for Palantir Foundry, Ontology, AIP, Gotham, Defense OSDK, Automate, Apollo and JupyterLab Code Workspaces across the XUNIA / ZYRA ecosystem, extended with a sovereignty-oriented memory/compute/GPU/performance model.

Foundry.role: governed ingestion, transforms, datasets, lineage and application data substrate

AIP.role: agent reasoning, LLM workflows, automations and evals

Ontology.role: objects, links, properties, actions, functions and operational state

Gotham.role: authorized defense/intelligence operational workflows over dynamic ontology data

Defense OSDK.role: typed defense application SDK contract for intelligence, mission planning, order of battle and sustainment

Automate.role: event/time-driven effects using Ontology Actions and AIP Logic

JupyterLab.role: Foundry Code Workspace for analysis, models, notebooks and Ontology interaction
requires: AIP enabled for AIP coding agent

sovereignty_reference_model.interpretation_rule: Use the visual as an architecture reference for GPT-DOUG. Do not treat visual labels alone as proof of tenant capability, licensing, deployment, or control over Palantir infrastructure.

layers_bottom_to_top.name: Data Sovereignty
layers_bottom_to_top.gpt_doug_mapping: governed datasets, durable evidence, lineage, retention, source ownership

layers_bottom_to_top.name: Compute & Logic Sovereignty
layers_bottom_to_top.gpt_doug_mapping: local CPU/GPU routing, bounded functions, deterministic transforms, workload policy

layers_bottom_to_top.name: Model Sovereignty
layers_bottom_to_top.gpt_doug_mapping: provider-neutral model routing, open/closed model choice, version/eval provenance

layers_bottom_to_top.name: Semantic Sovereignty
layers_bottom_to_top.gpt_doug_mapping: Ontology objects, links, properties, entity identity and shared meaning

layers_bottom_to_top.name: Kinetic Sovereignty
layers_bottom_to_top.gpt_doug_mapping: Actions and effects remain explicitly permissioned, observable, reviewable and reversible where possible

layers_bottom_to_top.name: Application Sovereignty
layers_bottom_to_top.gpt_doug_mapping: operator-owned applications and browser/OSDK clients using governed interfaces

layers_bottom_to_top.name: Knowledge Sovereignty
layers_bottom_to_top.gpt_doug_mapping: information -> reasoning -> action -> consequences with provenance and feedback converted back into governed knowledge

memory.goal: fast recall without allowing cache state to become authority
tiers: L2 local persisted indexes/checkpoints where explicitly enabled
L3 governed Ontology/dataset/evidence source of truth
rules: cache may accelerate reads but never silently override authoritative governed state
cache entries are disposable and bounded
sensitive data follows the source system's authorization and retention requirements

compute.goal: route each workload to the least expensive capable compute path
local_backends: mlx on supported Apple-silicon environments when installed
rules: detect capability at runtime instead of assuming a GPU exists
bound concurrency to available local CPU capacity
do not represent local hardware detection as control of Foundry compute

gpu.goal: accelerate model/tensor workloads only when the installed runtime can actually use the device
measurement: model-specific tokens-per-second when a model runner is attached

speed.goal: reduce repeated work before adding hardware
mechanisms: TTL/LRU caching for repeat knowledge and Ontology reads
network round-trip and API latency telemetry
speed.truthfulness_rule: A microbenchmark is only a local regression signal. Do not equate it with model tokens/second, Foundry performance, or GPU throughput.

routing_policy: Use Foundry for governed ingestion, transforms, lineage and application data.
Use AIP for model-assisted reasoning and agent workflows.
Use the Ontology as the governed operational source of truth rather than unmanaged agent memory.
Use local cache only as a disposable acceleration layer; invalidate or refresh it when authoritative state changes.
Detect CPU/GPU capability at runtime and keep a CPU fallback instead of assuming accelerator availability.
Use Gotham only for data and workflows exposed to the authorized Gotham enrollment.
Use Defense OSDK only through tenant-generated typed clients and the invoking identity's permissions.
Do not expose autonomous local targeting-and-fires execution; represent such data only where authorized for read-only context, simulation or review.
Use Automate for bounded event/time workflows; stage consequential effects for human review where policy requires.
Use Apollo for governed software delivery, never as ambient remote execution authority.
Use JupyterLab Code Workspaces for exploratory analysis, model development and notebook-based Ontology work.
Re-authorize every cross-plane action and preserve identity, markings, provenance and audit logs.
Measure speed with workload-specific evidence; never infer Foundry or GPU performance from a generic local benchmark.
truthfulness_rule: Configuration flags, architecture mappings, local accelerator detection and benchmark results describe intended integration or local runtime state only. They never imply Palantir licensing, enrollment, entitlement, credentials, connectivity, government affiliation, mission authority, weapons-release authority, control of Palantir infrastructure, or a performance guarantee.

terminology.jupiter: Normalized to JupyterLab because current Palantir documentation exposes JupyterLab through Code Workspaces; no Palantir product named Jupiter was verified.
